newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-FOUR-GOAL FOWLER PUTS LIVERPOOL BACK IN TITLE HUNT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FOUR-GOAL FOWLER PUTS LIVERPOOL BACK IN TITLE HUNT.

text.p: Robbie Fowler steered Liverpool's title challenge back on course when he scored four times in his side's 5-1 destruction of Middlesbrough in the English premier league on Saturday.

The 21-year-old Liverpool-born striker, who ironically supported Everton as a boy, also chalked up his 100th goal for the club in only 165 appearances -- one match less than it took former Anfield idol Ian Rush.

His outstanding individiual performance -- his fist goal came after only 29 seconds -- and Liverpool's superb team play showed the Reds had quickly got last week's shock 1-0 home defeat by Sheffield Wednesday out of their system.

Middlesbrough were never in with a chance after falling behind so early and were always second best in their 12th league match without victory. Despite the return of unsettled Brazilian Emerson, Middlesbrough never troubled the home side and as each week goes by they look a safer bet for relegation.
Fowler made it 2-0 with his 100th goal after 28 minutes and then spent the next 60 seconds showing off his T-shirt to his team-mates which read: "Job's A Good 'Un."
Norwegian Stig Inge Bjornebye got a third before half-time with Fowler adding two more after the break to complete Middlesbrough's misery.

Stan Collymore, recalled in place of flu-victim Patrik Berger, made four of Liverpool's goals while a Jan-Age Fjortoft header, which took a deflection off Liverpool's Michael Thomas was Middlesbrough's only spot of joy from a miserable afternoon.

The victory moved Liverpool onto 34 points, a point behind leaders Arsenal, who did not play, and left them level with Wimbledon, who ended Blackburn's five-match unbeaten run with a 1-0 win at Selhurst Park.
It was an uninspiring match but the London side managed to stretch their unbeaten run to 19-matches courtsey of a winner five minutes from time time from substitute Dean Holdsworth.
The goal came when he rammed the ball home from close range after Neil Ardley knocked down a cross from Peter Fear.
The only other match played on Saturday was a goalless draw between Leeds and Tottenham at Elland Road.

Some of the most heated action occured before the match when angry Leeds fans yelled abuse at Tottenham's new signing John Scales, who turned down Leeds last Sunday to instead join Spurs from Liverpool. Scales was expected to make his debut, but Tottenham manager Gerry Francis left him out because he was not fully match fit.
Both sides had chances to score but failed to take them with Tottenham's David Howells going closest when he headed against the bar with Leeds keeper Nigel Martyn well beaten.
